title: Itemized billing & refund protocol for cancellable rerank pipelines with shared prefetch cache
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Non-chat endpoints that perform embeddings + rerank often prefetch candidate embeddings (speculative prefetch) and fan out to third-party or internal tool executions. When the caller cancels, or when a later-stage rerank short-circuits candidates, we currently either overcharge for prefetched items or under-account for partially executed tool calls. This ticket designs and implements an itemized billing and refund protocol that attributes cost precisely across prefetch, executed rerank, and cancelled tool executions while respecting tenant quotas and rate limits.

Goals:
1) Ensure customers are billed only for actual execution cost with deterministic refunds/credits for cancelled or superseded work.
2) Maintain strong invariants for quota consumption so that rate-limits and daily quotas reflect usable capacity (no double-charging units already rolled back).
3) Keep attribution explainable in customer invoices and console drilldowns (per-candidate provenance).
4) Limit runtime latency/regressions and keep implementation incremental with clear fallbacks.

Scope: Embeddings prefetch + rerank pipelines on non-chat endpoints, including structured tool invocations triggered by rerank. Excludes chat multi-turn token accounting (handled in other tickets).
notes: Design idea: introduce a two-phase metering fence per request: a soft reservation recorded in metadata (cheap, not charged) and a commit step at the point of actual execution where tokens/units are consumed and billed.

Refund semantics: aborted soft reservations are removed with a negative delta emitted to accounting; partially executed toolcalls result in prorated commit amounts and per-tool execution logs for auditability.
KV-cache interaction: prefetched embeddings stored in shared prefix cache must not cause billing; only cache misses that trigger encoder runtime should be billed at commit time.
Quota rule: reservations decrement a 'reserved' counter but do not reduce 'available' quota until commit completes; concurrent requests see reserved capacity to prevent oversubscription.
Trade-offs: holding reservations increases quota state complexity and small risk of fragmentation; mitigation: TTL-based reservation expiry + periodic compactor job.
Performance: commit path is optimized via batched accounting writes and idempotency keys to tolerate duplicate commits from retry paths.
acceptance_criteria: New flow records a soft reservation for each prefetched candidate without generating billable units.
When a candidate is executed, a commit event is emitted and the exact token/compute units are charged; console shows per-candidate line items in the request trace.
Cancelled requests or superseded candidates generate a deterministic refund/credit entry within 2 minutes and reduce 'reserved' counters; no customer is billed for cancelled-only prefetches.
Quota accounting reflects reservations and commits: rate-limiter prevents oversubscription even under heavy speculative prefetch workloads.
End-to-end tests covering normal commit, duplicate commit, cancel-before-commit, partial tool failures, and reservation expiry pass in CI.
Metrics: see rollout plan metrics achieved (billing delta, refund latency, quota oversubscription rate).
comments: 2025-02-12 10:34 - Ava Martinez: Created initial draft. Problem observed in customer-support ticket about refunds not appearing after cancelled rerank jobs.
2025-02-14 15:07 - Liam Chen: Spike completed validating reservation TTL approach; shared cache emit semantics clarified (cache inserts are meta-only). See design doc link.
2025-02-18 09:22 - Priya Gupta (PM): Reviewed and requested clearer customer-facing invoice wording and example flows for docs team.
2025-02-21 16:51 - Marco Alvarez (SRE): Flagged compactor job must be rate-limited to avoid DB hot-writes during heavy traffic; suggested batched GC window of 30s.
2025-02-25 11:03 - Engineering Review: Decided to implement in two milestones: (1) reservation+commit API + offline reconciler, (2) real-time refund emitter + console UI.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable reservation+commit for 10% of requests on hosted API for low-volume tenants; monitor refund anomalies and quota behavior.
Phase 2 (expanded): enable for all non-chat rerank endpoints; expose conservative console indicators; keep real-time refunds disabled (use reconciler).
Phase 3 (final): enable real-time refund emission and update billing pipeline; switch reconciler to auditing-only mode.
Rollback: feature flag to disable reservation gating and fall back to legacy full-charge semantics; automated reconciler to convert soft reservations into noop and issue compensating credits.
test_plan: Unit: reservation lifecycle, idempotent commit, duplicate commit, cancel-before-commit negative delta.
Integration: simulated rerank pipeline with 1000 prefetched candidates including random cancels; assert billing ledger matches expected commits and refunds.
E2E: end-to-end for a sample customer showing invoice line items for requests with prefetch-only, prefetch+commit, and prefetch+partial-tool-execution.
Load: stress test reservation churn and compactor GC under 10k rps to ensure DB write SLOs.
metrics: Billing delta (difference vs legacy method) <= 0.5% after Phase 2
Quota oversubscription incidents reduced to 0 per million requests
Reservation TTL compactor CPU < 5% of billing job budget
